newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two key suspects in Japan subway case arrested - TV.
newsitem.headline: Two key suspects in Japan subway case arrested - TV.

text.p: Japanese police have arrested two key suspects in last year's Tokyo subway gas attack, both of them members of the doomsday cult accused of the gassing, television reports said on Thursday.

Koichi Kitamura, one of 10 members of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) alleged to have carried out the sarin nerve gas attack, was one of those arrested, the TBS and Fuji television networks reported.
Twelve people died and thousands were made ill by the subway attack, which took place on March 20, 1995. Shoko Asahara, the guru of the sect, is on trial for masterminding the attack.
The reports said the two men gave themselves up to the police.
The other suspect arrested was Zenji Yagisawa, who police allege was involved in an attempted cyanide gas attack in Tokyo's entertainment district of Shinjuku on May 5 last year.
Yagisawa is suspected of installing a crude home-made device to release cyanide in a toilet in an underground shopping mall. A cleaner found the device before it went off and it was defused.
